entries.title: Prefer online
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. Use a valid online route when it succeeds. If it is unavailable or fails, try the downloaded offline route once. Default: this setting, with Offline maps only off. The built maps row keeps a general feature description; geographic readiness is shown after opening it. Mapbox retains its configured-key status, with optional wording in strict mode.

entries.title: Prefer offline
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. Try a usable local route first. Missing coverage/data, a local failure, or no route triggers one online attempt if online routing is usable. The built maps row keeps a general feature description; geographic readiness is shown after opening it. Mapbox retains its configured-key status, with optional wording in strict mode.

entries.title: Offline maps only
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. No online routing request and no online routing fallback. Preferred maps is disabled and remembers its prior selection for when the override is turned off. Search remains a separate online feature. The built maps row keeps a general feature description; geographic readiness is shown after opening it. Mapbox retains its configured-key status, with optional wording in strict mode.

entries.title: Offline only, maps missing
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. Keep the strict choice. The Offline Maps row leads to the existing region panes to obtain the missing maps. Do not silently use online routing. The built maps row keeps a general feature description; geographic readiness is shown after opening it. Mapbox retains its configured-key status, with optional wording in strict mode.

entries.title: A · One selection downloads all missing maps
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. One region selection and one Download action. Add its 280 MiB routing data without redownloading the road data. Software setup happens as part of Prepare, with no separate user step. Region labels use real catalog availability in production; Iowa and Illinois routing is currently published. The mock has illustrative coverage elsewhere. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header.

entries.title: Existing U.S. region groups
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. Use the same catalog and summary for multi-state coverage. The available routing package must cover the selection as a connected graph; unsupported combinations are not labelled ready. Region labels use real catalog availability in production; Iowa and Illinois routing is currently published. The mock has illustrative coverage elsewhere. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header.

entries.title: Existing country pane
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. The same flow handles countries. Catalog availability shown here is illustrative; the small Liechtenstein graph was used for the standalone trial. Region labels use real catalog availability in production; Iowa and Illinois routing is currently published. The mock has illustrative coverage elsewhere. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header.

entries.title: A region without routing coverage
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. Show the limitation in the same pane. Road data may still download. Offline maps only never falls back online, so it cannot route there until coverage is provided. Region labels use real catalog availability in production; Iowa and Illinois routing is currently published. The mock has illustrative coverage elsewhere. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header.

entries.title: One Offline Maps page
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. The existing maps page shows both data types, a shared update schedule and Choose regions. No routing-software or URL page is needed. The existing global Remove maps action removes both datasets; per-region deletion is not exposed by mapd. Settings footer and device-wide storage bar are retained. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header.

entries.title: Prepare in the current layout
entries.note: Matches the approved progress layout in the native device capture. Keep the current percentage, bar, four steps, region tiles, footer and background-download message. Both map sets are included automatically. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Offline routes, current progress layout
entries.note: Matches the approved progress layout in the native device capture. Restore the existing large percentage, single bar and region grid. The small Offline routes label scopes this percentage to routing bytes, while a short line confirms road data is ready. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Road data, same progress screen
entries.note: Matches the approved progress layout in the native device capture. Keep the existing file count and region tile. Offline routes follow automatically in the same screen. The phase label and percentage reset explicitly when switching datasets; do not average file counts and bytes. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Multiple regions, familiar tiles
entries.note: Superseded by the approved valhalla4 shared-progress states: per-region transfer counters, measured installation and a completed Ready check. Matches the approved progress layout in the native device capture. Keep the current seven-column region grid, completed/current/waiting colors and per-region percentage. A green region means both required map sets are installed; the top percentage describes the labelled download phase. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Install keeps the existing step
entries.note: Superseded by the approved valhalla4 shared-progress states: per-region transfer counters, measured installation and a completed Ready check. Matches the approved progress layout. Keep Install as step three. Download at 100% is not Ready: the region remains current until its maps are checked and installed. The second capture applies the same approved screen to a local selection rebuild with zero new download bytes. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Retry in the same layout
entries.note: Matches the approved progress layout in the native device capture. Retain the last reported routing percentage, show the affected region in amber and replace the header action with Retry download. Retry only missing data; keep existing maps. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Ready in the same layout
entries.note: Superseded by the approved valhalla4 shared-progress states: per-region transfer counters, measured installation and a completed Ready check. Matches the approved progress layout in the native device capture. Advance the existing steps to Ready and turn the region green. Done returns to Offline Maps. No new management screen is introduced. The built screen retains the shared settings footer/page header. Time remaining appears only after a measured download rate exists.

entries.title: Remove both map sets
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. The existing global Remove maps action removes both datasets after confirmation. Saved places remain. The mock’s Remove region caption becomes Remove maps because mapd has no per-region tile ownership/deletion interface. The complete storage bar and shared settings footer are retained.

entries.title: Recalculating route
entries.note: Chip placement and time/street layout match in the native device capture. Use the existing bottom-left status-chip placement and dark fill. Keep the time, distance-left and live street in the normal bottom bar. Hide stale turn guidance independently. The road background is synthetic; existing button/control state is retained.

entries.title: Online failed; offline route works

entries.title: Offline failed; online route works
entries.note: Chip placement and time/street layout match in the native device capture. Using online maps appears briefly in the same chip. This state must never occur with Offline maps only on. The road background is synthetic; existing button/control state is retained.

entries.title: Offline only, route unavailable

This example has no previous route estimate, so the time fields show dashes while the available street stays visible. The road background is synthetic; existing button/control state is retained.

entries.title: Waiting for GPS

Last useful trip estimates may remain visible; they must not be treated as valid turn guidance. This mock illustrates a short interruption. The road background is synthetic; existing button/control state is retained.

entries.title: Routing and existing statuses together

Routing is informational and yields to safety alerts; it does not replace or recolor steering warnings. The road background is synthetic; existing button/control state is retained.

entries.title: First route, no previous estimate

entries.title: Same maps entry from saved places
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. The footer opens the same Offline Maps and region selection flow as Navigation. No separate package manager or URL-entry flow.

entries.title: Offline-only preview needs maps
entries.note: Native device capture with sample data. Start stays disabled. Choose regions opens the existing region panes, rather than offering an online route or asking for a package URL.

entries.title: Device › RAM
entries.note: What was using RAM at the peak of each of the last three drives that ran low, with the Low on RAM chip's 85% hold: the picker of drives, the top five processes by PSS with a plain description, a bar against the largest, their size and their growth since a baseline a minute into the drive (amber from 50 MB), then other processes and the system. A red dot on RAM in the sidebar until it's opened; the section is hidden until a drive first runs low. Page ground uses true black (#000000).

entries.title: Onroad › Low RAM chip
entries.note: StarPilot's Low Memory notice (RAM, not storage) as a red Low on RAM chip instead of the bottom banner, in arrival order and the lowest priority. Fill, border, icon, text color and place match. The percentage is drawn in the label's color and weight, not bolder and whiter, so the sentence can be translated whole. Page ground uses true black (#000000). The second native capture verifies the owner-requested merge: routing precedes Low on RAM in priority, with RamWatch retaining its 85% clear threshold and the normal time/street bar.

entries.title: Shared US build · Apply the checked states

entries.title: Per-region download progress

entries.title: Measured shared installation
entries.note: Approved November 4; native device capture matches the layout and counters. Installation has its own measured counter. All selected regions are installed together and remain unready until activation. The built screen retains the shared settings header and footer.

entries.title: Measured final verification
entries.note: Approved November 4; native device capture matches the layout and counters. The same installation counter advances through logical graph verification. It is capped below 100% until activation. The built screen retains the shared settings header and footer.

entries.title: Both map sets ready
entries.note: Approved November 4; native device capture matches the layout and counters. All four steps, including Ready, and both state tiles have green checks only after verified activation. The built screen retains the shared settings header and footer. Paired road/routing updates now use the approved valhalla5 single-bar states; this remains the routing-only reference.

entries.title: Paired downloads · Starting at 0%

entries.title: Paired downloads · Iowa

Two routing workers overlap with the current state’s road downloader. Native device capture inspected beside the approved Chromium mock; layout, counters and wording match. The shared settings header/footer are retained.

entries.title: Paired downloads · Illinois
entries.note: Approved November 4. Both Iowa downloads have finished; Illinois is current at 18%. The single overall bar is 59%. Downloaded states await shared installation before receiving green checks. Native device capture inspected beside the approved Chromium mock; layout, counters and wording match. The shared settings header/footer are retained.

entries.title: Paired downloads · All maps ready
entries.note: Approved November 4. All maps ready uses the approved plain wording. All four steps and every region receive green checks after verified activation.
